Subject: Performance SLO qualification - latency/throughput targets (Acme AI)

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and cost levers: 

TL;DR: Acme needs sub-200ms median token latency for the 95th percentile of requests at peak (conversational streaming), sustain 120 qps across global region with bursts to 300 qps, and concurrency per session of up to 12. Goal: keep hosted unit cost within the target you referenced (~$0.003/token avg).

What we covered:
- Workload: streaming chat (server->client token-by-token streaming) with many short turns (~15 tokens avg per turn) and occasional long responses (~300 tokens).
- Targets: 95th pct latency target = 200ms; steady throughput = 120 qps; peak bursts = 300 qps; concurrency = 12.
- Data sensitivity: PII in user messages, want Private deployment option later.

Cost/performance levers we'll evaluate:
1) Continuous batching: groups small requests to increase GPU utilization — good for cost without huge latency impact if batching window kept tight.
2) KV / prefix caching: cache repeated prefixes across sessions to avoid redoing compute for system prompts and canned context.
3) Quantization profiles: 8-bit / 4-bit options for model variants; 4-bit may reduce cost but we need quality checks.
4) Model variants & routing: use a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical queries and keep high-fidelity model for critical responses / long-form generation.
5) Autoscaling and warm pools: reserve capacity for burst patterns to avoid cold-start latency.
6) Streaming optimizations: early-token pipelining + kernel selection tuned for short-turn streaming.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a draft SLO spreadsheet (slo_requirements.xlsx) for you to confirm traffic split (chat vs. async) and distribution of short vs. long responses.
- Rishi will run a quick internal estimate on expected token cost delta between 8-bit and 4-bit for your avg prompt lengths.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra/ML team to validate streaming implementation details and test KV cache boundaries.

Can you confirm the traffic distribution numbers in the attached sheet and share a preferred 2-hour window for a deep-dive next week?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the clear list of levers. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Targets: the 200ms is for token-to-token latency in streaming on the 95th pct; end-to-end response time can be up to 600ms for long responses, but we care most about first-byte and steady token latency.
- Traffic split: ~85% short turns (<=30 tokens), 15% long responses. Daily active qps closer to 90 qps average, but peak windows (US mornings + EU afternoons) could hit 300 qps for ~10-15 minutes.
- Concurrency: 12 concurrent sessions is accurate per user for our multi-tab flows.

A couple of asks: 
1) Can you surface expected tail-latency impact of batching windows at 5ms / 10ms / 20ms? We need to balance batching for cost vs tail-latency for UX.
2) Do you have any early guidance on quantization quality regressions for our use case (short chat + occasional long generations)?

We can do a deep-dive next Wednesday 2026-02-25 10:00–11:00 PT with our infra lead (Priya) and model infra folks. I'll attach our session-instrumentation doc after this thread.

— Jordan

Jordan — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

On batching windows and tail latency:
- 5ms window: minimal added tail (~+5–10ms observed for token latency at 95th) with smaller effective batches; decent cost improvement for extremely bursty short-turn workloads.
- 10ms window: better utilization, tail increases ~+15–25ms at 95th depending on qps distribution.
- 20ms window: significant utilization gains but tail could increase ~+30–60ms at 95th on short streams — still may be within your 200ms target for many cases but risky for very short token turnaround.

Quantization guidance:
- 8-bit (int8): very low regression risk for short-turn chat; good cost win.
- 4-bit (nf4 / q4): larger model-quality variance on long-form content and creative generation. If you route long responses to a higher-fidelity variant, 4-bit looks promising for bulk cost reduction.

Proposed experiment matrix for the deep-dive:
1) Baseline: FP16 model, no batching, warm pool sizing for peak 300 qps (measure token latency distribution).
2) Batch-window sweep: 0ms / 5ms / 10ms / 20ms with continuous batching enabled.
3) Cache test: enable KV caching for repeated system prompts — measure token savings and latency impact.
4) Quantization split: route 85% short-turn to 4-bit / 8-bit variant (A/B), keep 15% long-generation on FP16.

Attached a short deck (redwood-deploy-options.pdf) describing our routing and model-variant flows for split traffic.

Next steps:
- Confirm deep-dive: Wed 2026-02-25 10:00 PT works for us. I'll add Nikhil (APIs) and Rishi (cost modeling) to the invite.
